state.claim: The U.S. surgeon general and the Centers for Disease Control both previously said that ‘masks are not effective in preventing [the] general public from catching coronavirus.’

candidates.quote: "They are NOT effective in preventing general public from catching coronavirus, but if healthcare providers can't get them to care for sick patients, it puts them and our communities at risk!" he added.

U.S. Surgeon General Jerome Adams had initially advised against the general public wearing face masks, saying they were "not effective" in preventing people from contracting COVID-19 and amplified the risk of health-care providers being unable to get them.
"Seriously people — STOP BUYING MASKS!" Adams said via Twitter on Feb. 29.
However, Adams told NBC's "TODAY" show on Wednesday that he has now asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to investigate whether this recommendation should change.

* Wearing a mask and putting distance between yourself and others can help lower the risk of COVID-19 transmission.
* Testing for COVID-19 can help you decide what to do next, like getting treatment to reduce your risk of severe illness and taking steps to lower your chances of spreading COVID-19 to others.

COVID-19 pandemic control requires a multipronged application of evidence-based strategies while improving health equity: universal face mask use, physical distancing, avoiding nonessential indoor spaces, increasing testing, prompt quarantine of exposed persons, safeguarding those at increased risk for severe illness or death, protecting essential workers, postponing travel, enhancing ventilation and hand hygiene, and achieving widespread COVID-19 vaccination coverage.

passages.P2:
* U.S. Surgeon General Jerome Adams had initially advised against the general public wearing face masks.
* However, Adams told NBC's "TODAY" show on Wednesday that he has now asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to investigate whether this recommendation should change.
* To date, more than 938,000 people worldwide have contracted the coronavirus, with 47,273 deaths, according to data compiled by Johns Hopkins University.
passages.P3: People stand in line while wearing face masks in the Elmhurst neighborhood on April 1, 2020 in New York City.
passages.P5: America's top doctor appears to have softened his stance over the effectiveness of face masks when it comes to preventing the spread of the coronavirus.
passages.P6: U.S. Surgeon General Jerome Adams had initially advised against the general public wearing face masks, saying they were "not effective" in preventing people from contracting COVID-19 and amplified the risk of health-care providers being unable to get them.
passages.P7: "Seriously people — STOP BUYING MASKS!" Adams said via Twitter on Feb. 29.
passages.P8: "They are NOT effective in preventing general public from catching coronavirus, but if healthcare providers can't get them to care for sick patients, it puts them and our communities at risk!" he added.
passages.P9: However, Adams told NBC's "TODAY" show on Wednesday that he has now asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to investigate whether this recommendation should change.
passages.P10: He explained the advice to avoid wearing masks had been based on the "best available evidence at the time" but "we now know there is a significant amount of asymptomatic spread."
passages.P11: Adams also underlined three key points when it comes to wearing face masks, advising people to avoid touching their face, to save the N95 masks for health-care workers who need them and to continue following social distancing guidelines.
passages.P12: ## WHO's advice on when to wear a mask
passages.P13: To date, more than 938,000 people worldwide have contracted the coronavirus, with 47,273 deaths, according to data compiled by Johns Hopkins University.
passages.P14: The U.S., which has the most confirmed infections of any country worldwide, has reported over 216,000 cases of the coronavirus, with 5,137 deaths.
passages.P15: Earlier this week, President Donald Trump warned of a "very, very painful two weeks" as the White House said it now projects the pandemic could claim the lives of between 100,000 to 240,000 Americans.
passages.P18: Trump on coronavirus: 'This is going to be a very painful two weeks'
passages.P19: The WHO states on its website that "if you are healthy, you only need to wear a mask if you are taking care of a person with suspected 2019-nCoV infection."
passages.P20: The United Nations health agency added masks were "effective only when used in combination with frequent hand-cleaning with alcohol-based hand rub or soap and water."
passages.P21: David Heymann, who led WHO's infectious disease unit at the time of the SARS epidemic in 2002-2003, said at a Chatham House briefing Wednesday that the WHO was also due to reconsider its guidance on wearing face masks following new evidence from Hong Kong, according to The Guardian.
passages.P22: The evidence was provided to the WHO confidentially, Heymann said, but it was likely to be made publicly available in due course.
passages.P25: Couple quarantined on cruise ship for their honeymoon

S2.title: How to Protect Yourself and Others | COVID-19 - CDC
S2.retrieval_query: What primary records, guidance documents, or official statements show what the CDC said about masks and the general public's risk of catching coronavirus, and on what date?

passages.P1: # How to Protect Yourself and Others
passages.P5:
* CDC’s Respiratory Virus Guidance provides strategies you can use to help protect yourself and others from health risks caused by COVID-19 and other respiratory viruses.
* These actions can help you lower the risk of COVID-19 transmission (spreading or catching COVID-19) and lower the risk of severe illness if you get sick.
passages.P7: CDC recommends that all people use core prevention strategies to protect themselves and others from COVID-19:
passages.P8:
* Stay up to date with COVID-19 vaccines.
  + Although vaccinated people sometimes get infected with the virus that causes COVID-19, staying up to date on COVID-19 vaccines significantly lowers the risk of getting very sick, being hospitalized, or dying from COVID-19.
* Practice good hygiene (practices that improve cleanliness)
* Take steps for cleaner air
passages.P10:
* Use precautions to prevent spread, including staying home and away from others (including people you live with who are not sick) if you have respiratory symptoms.
  + Learn when you can go back to your normal activities.
* Seek health care promptly for testing and/or treatment if you have risk factors for severe illness. Treatment may help lower your risk of severe illness, but it needs to be started within a few days of when your symptoms begin.
passages.P12: In addition, there are other prevention strategies that you can choose to further protect yourself and others.
passages.P13:
* Wearing a mask and putting distance between yourself and others can help lower the risk of COVID-19 transmission.
* Testing for COVID-19 can help you decide what to do next, like getting treatment to reduce your risk of severe illness and taking steps to lower your chances of spreading COVID-19 to others.
passages.P15: Using these prevention strategies can be especially helpful when:
passages.P16:
* Respiratory viruses, such as COVID-19, flu, and RSV, are causing a lot of illness in your community
* You or those around you have risk factors for severe illness
* You or those around you were recently exposed to a respiratory virus, are sick, or are recovering
passages.P18: Find out if respiratory viruses are causing a lot of illness in your community. Data updated weekly.
